added.title: Environmental Data Validator
added.description:
Position Description & Qualifications

Environmental Data Review & Validation Chemist

Serco is seeking an Environmental Data Review & Validation Chemist
to support the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency’s Laboratory Services and Applied Science Division (LSASD) in Fort Meade, Maryland.

As a member of Serco’s Environmental Service Assistance Team, you will collaborate with EPA scientists and staff to review and validate Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data. Your work will directly support the EPA’s mission to protect human health and the environment.

Serco offers a collaborative environment with opportunities to expand your technical knowledge, strengthen your analytical skills, and contribute to meaningful environmental initiatives.

In This Role, You Will

Review and validate organic analytical data, including volatile organic compounds, semivolatile organic compounds, pesticides, PCBs, dioxins, and PCB congeners, using applicable EPA National Functional Guidelines and regional standard operating procedures.
Validate metals data generated using inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) and inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) in accordance with applicable National Functional Guidelines.
Prepare detailed, accurate, and professional reports documenting data-review findings.
Manage and maintain electronic analytical data across multiple platforms.
Monitor workflows, backlogs, deliverables, and performance metrics.
Review standard operating procedures as needed.
Track and analyze key performance indicators to identify trends and support continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications

To be successful in this role, you must have:

A bachelor’s degree in chemistry or a related scientific field.
At least two years of experience working in environmental laboratories or with EPA analytical methods. An advanced degree may substitute for some professional experience.
At least one year of experience reviewing and validating analytical data.
Extensive experience performing gas chromatography (GC) or gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) analyses using one or more of the following:
EPA Contract Laboratory Program Statements of Work
EPA SW-846 methods
EPA drinking-water methods
Other applicable organic or inorganic analytical methods

Proficiency with Microsoft Office 365.
The ability to obtain an EPA Public Trust clearance.
Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills.
A solid background in analyzing and interpreting scientific data.

Preferred Qualifications

The following experience and skills are preferred:

At least three years of experience working as an organic or inorganic chemist or laboratory technician.
Experience with laboratory quality-control programs and analytical data review or validation.
Experience reviewing or analyzing one or more of the following:
Dioxins and PCB congeners using high-resolution gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (HRGC-MS)
Metals using ICP-AES or ICP-MS
Mercury using cold vapor analysis
Classical inorganic parameters, including hexavalent chromium, total organic carbon, total dissolved solids, total suspended solids, total solids, or cyanide

Experience writing technical reports, data-review narratives, standard operating procedures, or similar scientific documentation.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work extensively at a computer using a monitor and keyboard.
Flexibility to work evenings or weekends when required.

In North America, Serco’s 9,000+ employees strive to make an impact every day across 100+ sites in the areas of Defense, Citizen Services, and Transportation. We help our clients deliver vital services more efficiently while increasing the satisfaction of their end customers. Serco serves every branch of the U.S. military, numerous U.S. Federal civilian agencies, the Intelligence Community, the Canadian government, state, provincial and local governments, and commercial clients. added.title: Waste, Hazardous Materials & Remediation Coordinator
added.description:
Description

Company Summary:

Fermi America is pioneering the development of next-generation energy infrastructure to power the future of artificial intelligence. By delivering highly reliable, gigawatt-scale power solutions, we are helping meet the rapidly growing energy demands of advanced AI technologies. Our flagship HyperGrid™ campus in Amarillo, Texas, is designed to become one of the world's largest energy-driven AI complexes, integrating nuclear, natural gas, utility, solar, and battery power. With a planned 17 gigawatts of power capacity and 18 million square feet of AI infrastructure, Fermi America is positioned to play a leading role in the future of energy and artificial intelligence. At Fermi America, we are building more than infrastructure. We are creating opportunities for talented professionals to help shape the next generation of energy and AI innovation.

Job Summary

Fermi America is seeking a hands-on and safety-minded Waste, Hazardous Materials & Remediation Coordinator
to own solid and hazardous waste, hazardous materials, emergency release reporting, storage tanks, PCBs, asbestos, and legacy contamination at Project Matador. Reporting to the Environmental Manager, this role will run the site's RCRA generator program, lead spill response and agency release notifications, and manage soil and contamination issues on former Pantex Ordnance Plant land. The Waste, Hazardous Materials & Remediation Coordinator will work directly with contractors and vendors and deliver the site's waste, DOT, HAZWOPER, and spill-response training. The ideal candidate brings practical experience owning a hazardous waste program on construction or industrial sites, documented spill response, and the confidence to hold contractors to standard.

Responsibilities

RCRA: Manage the hazardous waste program under 40 CFR 260–279 and 30 TAC 335, including monthly generator-status determinations, TCEQ Form 00002 registration and EPA ID before the first shipment, waste characterization and Texas waste classification, weekly accumulation-area inspections, contingency plan and emergency coordinator duties (40 CFR 262.16–262.17), manifests and e-Manifest, universal waste (40 CFR 273), used oil (40 CFR 279), vendor qualification, and waste minimization.
DOT: Serve as a trained shipping-paper signer (49 CFR 172, Subpart H).
Emergency response and notification: Lead spill response and documentation; make CERCLA 103 and EPCRA 304 release notifications and Texas spill reports (30 TAC 327); maintain the 24-hour call tree.
Hazardous materials: Manage chemical approval, the Safety Data Sheet library, EPCRA Tier II reporting, and TRI readiness for operations.
Storage tanks: Manage petroleum storage tank (UST/AST) registration and compliance (30 TAC 334); conduct field SPCC inspections and maintain spill-kit readiness in support of the Water Resources Manager.
PCBs: Identify, manage, and dispose of PCB-containing equipment under TSCA (40 CFR 761), particularly legacy electrical equipment.
Asbestos and lead: Manage pre-demolition surveys, Texas Department of State Health Services notifications, abatement oversight, and disposal.
Legacy contamination: Implement the soil management plan and munitions stop-work triggers on former Pantex Ordnance Plant land; support Phase II assessments and Texas Risk Reduction Program (30 TAC 350) remediation.
Training: Deliver RCRA, DOT, HAZWOPER, and spill-response training.
Contractor compliance: Enforce the Contractor Environmental Compliance Manual (ENV-STD-001) and the pre-mobilization gate, with stop-work authority for environmental noncompliance.
On-call: Participate in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events, including notifications required within 24 hours.
Audits: Conduct media-specific audits of the role's own program and support the site's multimedia audit program.
Records: Keep all program records producible to an agency inspector within 24 hours.

Requirements

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science or a related field, or equivalent work experience.
Minimum of 4 years of hazardous waste management experience on construction or industrial sites.
Working knowledge of RCRA, 30 TAC 335, and DOT hazardous materials requirements.
Current 40-hour HAZWOPER certification.
Experience with release reporting.
OSHA 10-hour certification (OSHA 30-hour preferred).
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Microsoft Teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Certified Hazardous Materials Manager (CHMM).
Texas Risk Reduction Program (TRRP) remediation experience.
Munitions-response awareness.
PCB or asbestos program experience.
English/Spanish bilingual ability.

Work Environment & Travel

The position is based on site at Project Matador near Amarillo, Texas.
Participation in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events is required.
The role may involve work near legacy contamination and potential munitions on former Pantex Ordnance Plant land, under site protocols.
Site work requires walking active construction areas in all weather conditions and wearing required personal protective equipment.
Flexibility to support agency inspections, permit deadlines, and critical project milestones is expected.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Fermi America is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified applicants with disabilities throughout the hiring process.

added.description:
Description

Company Summary:

Fermi America is pioneering the development of next-generation energy infrastructure to power the future of artificial intelligence. By delivering highly reliable, gigawatt-scale power solutions, we are helping meet the rapidly growing energy demands of advanced AI technologies. Our flagship HyperGrid™ campus in Amarillo, Texas, is designed to become one of the world's largest energy-driven AI complexes, integrating nuclear, natural gas, utility, solar, and battery power. With a planned 17 gigawatts of power capacity and 18 million square feet of AI infrastructure, Fermi America is positioned to play a leading role in the future of energy and artificial intelligence. At Fermi America, we are building more than infrastructure. We are creating opportunities for talented professionals to help shape the next generation of energy and AI innovation.

Job Summary

Fermi America is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Environmental Specialist – Field Compliance, Natural & Cultural Resources, and Records
to serve as the environmental program's eyes on the ground and keeper of the record at Project Matador. Reporting to the Environmental Manager, this role will inspect every active work area across all environmental media, own wildlife, cultural resources, and pesticide oversight, track NRC environmental commitments in the field, administer the compliance database and training records, and run the audit schedule. The ideal candidate brings environmental field experience, strong recordkeeping habits, and a willingness to work outdoors on an active construction site.

Responsibilities

Field verification: Inspect every active work area weekly across all media, perform qualified stormwater inspections, and track corrective actions through closure.
Wildlife: Coordinate pre-clearing surveys and area releases with the contract biologist under the Endangered Species Act and Migratory Bird Treaty Act, including nesting birds, migratory waterfowl at the playas, and burrowing owls. Protect state-listed species such as the Texas horned lizard, manage prairie dog colonies as owl habitat, and maintain rattlesnake and wildlife-encounter protocols with HSSE.
Cultural resources and NEPA: Manage Antiquities Code of Texas notices, Section 106 commitments (36 CFR 800), the unanticipated-discovery plan, and field tracking of NRC Environmental Impact Statement commitments (10 CFR 51).
Pesticides and herbicides: Oversee vegetation and pest-control contractors under FIFRA, verify Texas Department of Agriculture applicator licensing and label compliance, and confirm general-permit coverage for any application to or over playa water.
Records and data: Administer the SharePoint compliance database and obligations register, automated deadline reminders, the 24-hour records-production drill, environmental data, and field instrument calibration.
Training: Deliver site environmental orientation in English and Spanish and maintain training records for all personnel.
Audits: Schedule and support media-specific, multimedia, and quality audits, including quarterly contractor audits under ENV-STD-001 and the independent third-party audit.
Contractor compliance: Enforce the Contractor Environmental Compliance Manual (ENV-STD-001) and the pre-mobilization gate, with stop-work authority for environmental noncompliance.
On-call: Participate in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events, including notifications required within 24 hours.

Requirements

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Biology, Geology, or a related field.
Minimum of 2–3 years of environmental field experience.
Strong recordkeeping and organizational skills.
Valid driver's license.
OSHA 10-hour certification (OSHA 30-hour preferred).
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Microsoft Teams.

Preferred Qualifications

CESSWI certification, or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire.
40-hour HAZWOPER certification.
Wildlife or cultural resource field experience.
SharePoint administration experience.
English/Spanish bilingual ability.

Work Environment & Travel

The position is based on site at Project Matador near Amarillo, Texas.
Participation in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events is required.
Field work includes wildlife surveys and encounters, including rattlesnakes, under HSSE protocols.
Site work requires walking active construction areas in all weather conditions and wearing required personal protective equipment.
Flexibility to support agency inspections, permit deadlines, and critical project milestones is expected.

Equal Employment Opportunity

added.title: Senior Environmental Specialist - Texas
added.description:
The Opportunity

Ulteig is seeking a full-time Senior Environmental Specialist to help grow and deliver environmental compliance services for public and private clients across our Transportation, Renewables, Power, and Water & Environment Lifeline Sectors, as well as other industries we serve. This is an opportunity for an experienced environmental consultant to apply their technical expertise, market knowledge, and professional relationships while working with Ulteig’s multidisciplinary teams to help clients navigate environmental compliance, permitting, and due diligence. We recognize that senior environmental professionals bring different areas of depth, and we are interested in candidates who can lead from their strengths, connect the right technical resources, and help shape how our services grow in Texas. The candidate will have flexibility to work from our Austin office and/or remotely from Texas.

The Senior Environmental Specialist will play a central role in building Ulteig’s existing environmental presence in Texas by developing new client opportunities and helping win additional work with Ulteig’s existing accounts. The successful candidate will leverage their professional network and market knowledge, collaborate with Ulteig’s environmental, market, and client teams, and lead pursuits from early client engagement through proposal and award. This includes developing responsive solutions, scopes, budgets, staffing plans, and delivery approaches that position Ulteig to win and successfully execute the work.

This is a seller-doer-builder role. The successful candidate will remain actively involved in billable project delivery and, as backlog grows, coordinate workload with the existing team, help recruit, mentor, and develop new team members needed to deliver workload. Relevant experience may include environmental planning and permitting, National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) compliance, biological and natural resources, waters and wetlands, environmental due diligence, historic and cultural resources, public or stakeholder involvement, or related environmental services. The successful candidate will bring meaningful depth in one or more areas, strong consulting judgment, and the ability to recognize project needs and bring together the appropriate resources to deliver successful outcomes.

The ideal candidate is a collaborative and self-directed consultant who can create structure, exercise sound judgment, and move projects and opportunities forward in a fast-paced environment. This person should be comfortable helping develop a growing regional practice while remaining connected to Ulteig’s broader technical teams, client relationships, and market strategies.

What You’ll Do

Leverage established professional networks and market knowledge to identify, develop, and secure new clients and project opportunities
Partner with Ulteig’s environmental, market, client, and technical teams to identify environmental needs, expand services within existing accounts, and pursue multidisciplinary opportunities
Build lasting client relationships through strategic advice, responsive service, and successful project delivery
Lead pursuit strategy and the preparation of proposals, scopes of services, schedules, budgets, staffing plans, and client presentations
Advise public and private clients on practical environmental compliance, permitting, and due diligence approaches, including regulatory coordination, permit acquisition, and ongoing compliance
Lead and manage multidisciplinary environmental projects, including project scope, schedule, budget, staffing, quality, and client communication
Provide technical leadership and contribute directly within areas of expertise while assembling and coordinating additional resources based on project needs
Plan and provide technical oversight for environmental studies, investigations, and field efforts, including data interpretation and preparation or review of reports, plans, permit applications, and related deliverables
Communicate environmental requirements, findings, risks, and recommendations clearly to clients, agencies, and multidisciplinary project teams
Mentor junior staff and help identify, recruit, and develop the team and technical resources needed to support regional growth

What We Expect From You

Bachelor's or advanced degree in environmental science, environmental planning, environmental policy, biology, wildlife management, range management, natural resources management, or related field
15+ years of related environmental consulting, compliance, permitting, or project-development experience
Demonstrated experience developing client relationships, identifying and pursuing opportunities, leading or contributing to successful pursuits, and converting client and market needs into project work
Established professional relationships and market knowledge in Texas and surrounding region, including relationships with clients, regulatory agencies, industry organizations, teaming partners, or prospective employees
Thorough understanding of relevant Federal, State, and Local environmental review, permitting, and compliance requirements, such as NEPA, Endangered Species Act, Clean Water Act; Clean Air Act, National Historic Preservation Act, Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act, Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
Strong oral and written communication, analytical, interpersonal, prioritization, and time-management skills
Ability to work independently while building effective relationships and collaborating across client, market, technical, and multidisciplinary teams
Ability to create structure, exercise sound judgment, and move opportunities and projects forward in a fast-paced, evolving environment
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Adobe Acrobat; familiarity with GIS, field-data collection, project management, or other technical tools
Willingness to travel as needed for client meetings, industry events, project delivery, and occasional fieldwork, including overnight stays
Demonstrates openness to innovation by embracing and applying evolving technology and AI tools to enhance workflows, solve problems, and drive continuous improvement.
Must have authorization to work permanently in the U.S.

As you consider applying for a position at Ulteig, we encourage you to think outside the box – because we do! You might not meet 100% of the skills listed in a description, but we are committed to hiring people with exceptional talent, ability, and potential, and then creating an environment where they can become the best versions of themselves. We don’t want to miss out on the possibility of speaking with the next outstanding Ulteig team members, so please apply if you think this role is a great match for your unique skills and strengths. And yes, relevant military experience is absolutely considered for transitioning service members.

What You Can Expect From Ulteig

Ulteig is a purpose-driven organization that has built a culture focused on people, both our clients and our employees, for over 80 years. Working at Ulteig is more than a job, opening opportunities to make an impact by creating and solving for a sustainable future. We recognize our success relies heavily on the dedication and focus of our workforce; this is why we make investing in our employees a top priority. We prioritize flexibility and staying connected to meeting your needs and helping you achieve your goals. We value your unique perspective, respect your individuality, and celebrate your contributions. At Ulteig, we take our success and the success of our clients personally.

Ulteig is a trusted partner in engineering North America’s essential infrastructure and leverages its expertise with a wide range of public and private clients.

At Ulteig, we care deeply about our team, listening to their needs and ensuring they have the tools necessary to be productive, whether they choose to work remotely, hybrid, or in the office. Regardless of where you work, you are empowered to build a workday that best suits your strengths. We strive to ensure a balance and separation between home and work life. added.description:
Description

Company Summary:

Fermi America is pioneering the development of next-generation energy infrastructure to power the future of artificial intelligence. By delivering highly reliable, gigawatt-scale power solutions, we are helping meet the rapidly growing energy demands of advanced AI technologies. Our flagship HyperGrid™ campus in Amarillo, Texas, is designed to become one of the world's largest energy-driven AI complexes, integrating nuclear, natural gas, utility, solar, and battery power. With a planned 17 gigawatts of power capacity and 18 million square feet of AI infrastructure, Fermi America is positioned to play a leading role in the future of energy and artificial intelligence. At Fermi America, we are building more than infrastructure. We are creating opportunities for talented professionals to help shape the next generation of energy and AI innovation.

Job Summary

Fermi America is seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Water Resources Permitting & Compliance Manager
to own the stormwater, surface water, wastewater, drinking water, groundwater, and spill prevention programs for Project Matador. Reporting to the Environmental Manager, this role will keep construction stormwater controls inspection-ready across a large, active site, protect on-site playas, obtain the wastewater and drinking water authorizations the campus needs to operate, and own the SPCC program. The Water Resources Permitting & Compliance Manager will serve as Fermi America's primary point of contact with TCEQ on water matters. The ideal candidate brings strong Texas water permitting experience, hands-on stormwater compliance on large construction sites, and experience running sampling programs and managing laboratory data.

Responsibilities

Construction stormwater: Maintain TPDES coverage under TXR150000 and the SWP3, including outfalls, sediment basins, BMP installation, vehicle trackout controls, and concrete washout (40 CFR 450). Verify each contractor's NOI or site notice, and run the qualified-inspector program on the required 7-day or 14-day-plus-rain schedule.
Playas and surface water: Treat playas as water in the state (Texas Water Code 26.121). Develop and execute Sampling and Analysis Plans and QA/QC for playa water quality against the Texas Surface Water Quality Standards (30 TAC 307). Manage point and nonpoint source controls, wetlands, Section 404/401 and Nationwide Permits, and floodplain coordination.
Wastewater: Manage the Texas Land Application Permit, wastewater plant design approval (30 TAC 217), reclaimed water authorization (30 TAC 210), industrial and cooling-water authorizations, effluent standards, and Discharge Monitoring Reports. Oversee general permits for concrete production water (TXG110000) and hydrostatic test water (TXG670000), dewatering, interim pump-and-haul, and future industrial stormwater coverage.
Drinking water: Manage public water system approval under the Safe Drinking Water Act and 30 TAC 290, including sampling schedules, chain of custody, accredited laboratory analysis and transport, and public notification.
Groundwater and supply: Manage Panhandle Groundwater Conservation District well approvals, Texas Water Development Board water-use surveys (TWC 16.012), and groundwater protection near legacy Pantex conditions.
Spill prevention: Own the SPCC Plan (40 CFR 112), coordinate PE certification, conduct inspections, and train oil-handling personnel (40 CFR 112.7(f)).
Program management: Manage laboratory contracts, data validation, water consultants, and TCEQ inspections.
Contractor compliance: Enforce the Contractor Environmental Compliance Manual (ENV-STD-001) and the pre-mobilization gate, with stop-work authority for environmental noncompliance.
On-call: Participate in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events, including notifications required within 24 hours.
Audits: Conduct media-specific audits of the role's own program and support the site's multimedia audit program.
Training: Develop and deliver program-specific environmental training for employees and contractors.
Records: Keep all program records producible to an agency inspector within 24 hours.

Requirements

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Civil or Environmental Engineering, Hydrology, or a related field.
Minimum of 6 years of Texas water permitting and compliance experience.
Construction stormwater compliance experience on large sites.
Experience managing sampling programs and laboratory data.
SPCC program experience.
OSHA 10-hour certification (OSHA 30-hour preferred).
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Microsoft Teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Texas Professional Engineer (PE) license.
CPESC, CPSWQ, or CESSWI certification.
Public water system or TCEQ water operator experience.
West Texas groundwater or playa experience.
English/Spanish bilingual ability.

Work Environment & Travel

The position is based on site at Project Matador near Amarillo, Texas.
Participation in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events is required.
Field sampling and storm-event response are a regular part of the role.
Site work requires walking active construction areas in all weather conditions and wearing required personal protective equipment.
Flexibility to support agency inspections, permit deadlines, and critical project milestones is expected.

Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified applicants with disabilities throughout the hiring process.

Job Summary

Fermi America is seeking an experienced and technically strong Air Quality Permitting & Compliance Manager
to own every air authorization and air compliance obligation for Project Matador, from construction through commissioning and into operations. Reporting to the Environmental Manager, this role will maintain and amend the project's NSR/PSD/GHG PSD air permit, support the pending second air permit application, prepare the Title V and Acid Rain permit applications, and lead the continuous emissions monitoring program. The Air Quality Permitting & Compliance Manager will serve as Fermi America's primary point of contact with the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) on air matters. The ideal candidate brings deep TCEQ permitting experience on turbines or engines, hands-on CEMS and 40 CFR 75 experience, and the ability to build an air compliance program on a fast-moving greenfield project.

Responsibilities

Permits: Maintain and amend NSR/PSD/GHG PSD Permit 181009, support pending Application 183462, and protect the 18-month construction-start deadline (30 TAC 116.120). Manage standard permits and Permits by Rule (30 TAC 106), and verify contractor concrete batch plant registrations.
Federal programs: Prepare the Title V application (30 TAC 122; 40 CFR 70) and the Acid Rain permit application (40 CFR 72), which has a long lead time before first fire. Ensure compliance with NSPS (40 CFR 60, Subparts KKKa, IIII, JJJJ) and NESHAP standards (40 CFR 63, Subparts YYYY, ZZZZ), including 40 CFR 60.7 construction and startup notifications.
Continuous monitoring: Lead CEMS design review, certification, monitoring plans, RATAs, and QA/QC under 40 CFR 75 and 40 CFR 60 Appendices B and F; oversee stack testing and data acquisition and handling system reporting.
Technical analysis: Perform emissions calculations, BACT analyses, AERMOD ambient air modeling, and applicability determinations, including source aggregation of tenant backup generators.
Reporting: Prepare the Annual Emissions Inventory (30 TAC 101.10), deviation reports, Title V compliance certifications, and emissions event and maintenance reporting (30 TAC 101.201 and 101.211).
Construction air quality: Manage fugitive dust and opacity control, wind-speed stop-work triggers, and open-burning prohibitions (30 TAC 111); coordinate asbestos NESHAP notifications (40 CFR 61, Subpart M) with the Waste, Hazardous Materials & Remediation Coordinator.
Refrigerants: Manage refrigerant compliance for data center cooling systems (40 CFR 82, Subpart F), as applicable.
Program management: Lead air pollution prevention, design-change review, air consultant management, and TCEQ inspections.
Contractor compliance: Enforce the Contractor Environmental Compliance Manual (ENV-STD-001) and the pre-mobilization gate, with stop-work authority for environmental noncompliance.
On-call: Participate in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events, including notifications required within 24 hours.
Audits: Conduct media-specific audits of the role's own program and support the site's multimedia audit program.
Training: Develop and deliver program-specific environmental training for employees and contractors.
Records: Keep all program records producible to an agency inspector within 24 hours.

Required Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Environmental, Chemical, or Mechanical Engineering.
Minimum of 7 years of air permitting and compliance experience.
TCEQ NSR/PSD and Title V permitting experience on turbines or engines.
Hands-on CEMS and 40 CFR 75 experience.
NSPS and NESHAP compliance experience.
Strong technical writing skills.
OSHA 10-hour certification (OSHA 30-hour preferred).
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Microsoft Teams.

Preferred Qualification

Texas Professional Engineer (PE) license.
AERMOD dispersion modeling experience.
Experience supporting an Acid Rain Designated Representative.
Power generation or greenfield compliance program start-up experience.
English/Spanish bilingual ability.

Work Environment & Travel

The position is based on site at Project Matador near Amarillo, Texas.
Participation in a 24-hour on-call rotation for releases, emissions events, and storm events is required.
Occasional travel to TCEQ offices and other Fermi America locations may be required.
Site work requires walking active construction areas in all weather conditions and wearing required personal protective equipment.

Work closely with internal teams to develop and present proposals, technical solutions, and service offerings.
